name: AUX vs UX
caption:
Your next user might not have eyes.

I've been thinking about how much of what we design will be used by agents, not people. UX is about attention, hierarchy and emotion. AUX (agent experience) is about whether an agent can read your product, decide what to do and finish the task without guessing.

An agent works in a loop of read, decide, act and check, and each step is a design decision. Swipe through for what to get right at each one.

The worst failure isn't confusion, it's a silent wrong action. That's why permissions and confirmations matter as much as visuals.

Same goal as UX, different user. Which one are you designing for?

slides.headline: AUX vs UX

slides.descriptor: UX designs for a person: attention, hierarchy, emotion.
slides.headline: AUX designs for an agent that reads, decides and acts on its own.

slides.data:
| UX | AUX
Interface | Screens | Docs, APIs, schemas
Success | User understands | Agent completes the task
Clarity means | Visual hierarchy | Unambiguous structure
Failure | Confusion | Silent wrong action

slides.descriptor: Every step is a design decision.
slides.note: Repeats until the goal is met.

slides.descriptor: A person gets confused and leaves. An agent keeps going.
slides.headline: The worst failure is a silent wrong action.
slides.note: It books the wrong date and reports success. No error, no flag.

slides.data:
Read: One clear source of truth
Decide: Explicit options and limits
Act: Consistent tool names and inputs
Check: Errors that say what to fix

slides.headline: Your product has two users now. Which one are you designing for?
